statement.essentials: Inside the gland the trunk usually splits into an upper and a lower division.
statement.anatomy: At the pes anserinus the trunk usually divides into two, a temporofacial (upper) and a cervicofacial (lower) division; division into three is uncommon.
statement.clinical: Pooled prevalence of a bifurcated trunk was 94.1% in a meta-analysis of 2,453 nerves and 96.4% (trifurcation 3.2%) in a systematic review of 1,497 cases.

limitations: Studies classify the pattern differently; the authors note that the bifurcation is far more constant than the distal branching.
